InnovationName: Founder of Mission Working Dogs
InnovationDescription: opened Mission Working Dogs a non-profit in July 2020 in Oxford, Maine to provide service dogs to other Army vets; has written a few children's books; spearheaded the creation of an adaptive track and field program through Central Maine Adaptive Sports, a non-profit organization that offers adaptive sport opportunities like skiing, snowboarding, sled hockey, track and field and others; 2015 co-founded the New England Warriors sled hockey program, a sister program to the USA Warriors and is designed for the rehabilitation of ill and injured veterans;

InnovationName: Inventor of NasaClip
InnovationDescription: 2015 Founder & CEO of Nasa/Clip a medical device for nosebleeds
Invention: Bib; Nasal ice pack; Nasal compression device

InnovationName: Inventor of Shower Shirt
InnovationDescription: invented a shower shirt (patent # 8516613) that is water resistant to protect the chest of patients who have had chest surgery

InnovationName: Founder & CEO of MedAire Inc
InnovationDescription: 1985 founded MedAire Inc; 1987, founded MedLink; critical care flight nurse, telemed pioneer; offered the 1st global in-flight assistance program; founded a paramedic training program; author of One Life Lost, Millions Gained - The Story of a Flight Nurse Turned MedAire CEO;

InnovationName: Midwifery
InnovationDescription: midwife known for Gaskin Maneuver (also called all fours & the first obstetrical procedure to be named after a midwife), a technique she learned in Guatemala in 1976 for preventing & resolving shoulder dystocia during birth; 1971 with husband Stephen founded The Farm in Summerton Tennessee where they created The Farm Midwifery Center, one of the first out-of-hospital birthing centers in the United States; wrote Spiritual Midwifery (1977) & it is considered a seminal work on midwifery; between 1977 and 2000 published the quarterly magazine Birth Gazette (covered health care, childbirth, and midwifery issues); Ina May’s Guide to Childbirth, her second book about birth and midwifery, was published by Bantam/Dell in 2003; founder of the Safe Motherhood Quilt Project, a national effort developed to draw public attention to maternal death rates and to honor those women who have died of pregnancy-related causes since the 1980s; 1982 co-founder of Midwives Alliance of North America;

InnovationName: Considered to be 1st female law enforcement officer
InnovationDescription: 1908 was sworn in by the City of Portland as Superintendent of the Women's Auxiliary to the Police Department for the Protection of Girls (later renamed the Women's Protective Division) with the rank of detective after convincing the Mayor & city government officials of the need for the position; promoted laws to protect women, advised other jurisdictions about women's law-enforcement issues, and demonstrated by example that women could be effective police officers; 1904 was hired by several Portland Oregon charities & businesses (including Travelers aid & YWCA) to help protect young women expected to attend the 1905 Lewis & Clark Centennial Exposition from possible sexual exploitation by helping them find lodging, jobs, & safe environments during their stay in the city with a salary of $75 per month & the authority to make arrests; was one of 15 commissioners appointed to the Portland Vice Commission in 1911 to study the problem of venereal disease (VD) and its relation to the commercial sex trade; 1912 pushed for the creation of the Hillcrest Oregon Industrial School for Girls near Salem; 1918 obtained federal funding for the Cedars Venereal Detention Facility for Women near Portland;

InnovationName: Co-founder of MattersofTrust.org
InnovationDescription: 1998 co-founded the environmental public charity, Matter of Trust (MofT), with her husband Patrice Gautier (VP at Apple, Inc); 2000 started Hair Matters Program which collects and felts hair clippings into mats for oil spills and soil remediation; started TheHumSum.org, an environmental social media platform for Humanity Adding Solutions; started Eco-Industrial Hub, a working model factory with delightfully empowering and educational exhibits about clean air, water, energy, and ideal product materials; opened a Matter of Trust Eco-Center (2013) for field trips and roundtables; 1 of the co-founders of the Global Compost Project (2014); has written The Key in the Sea (2010) & The Prize in the Skies (2011); has written a children's book titled THE KEY IN THE SEA A PIPPEROOS SEA PLAY;

InnovationName: Co-founder of Monkey KIDS Sensor
InnovationDescription: a Manhasset NY mother who created a disposable beacon called Monkey KID Sensor that can be fastened to a child’s shoe in 2017 that pairs with a smartphone app that alerts parents when their children wander outside of a perimeter using geo-fencing technology & with her twin sister Renee Winiski created a company to manufacture & sell it; each beacon lasts approximately 4 months & the virtual fence can be set up to 170 feet wide; founded the Women in Data Science Symposia, providing a dynamic forum for female leaders to engage and address critical challenges within the sector; 2023 initiating the Executive Roundtable Series on Artificial Intelligence, bringing together industry thought leaders to explore AI's role in reshaping business and enterprise landscapes;

InnovationName: Inventor of early fire detection device
InnovationDescription: created a tool that uses thermal imaging to identify when a heat source (ie a gas burner) is left unattended for 10 minutes and alerts the resident but text message; founder & CEO Vigil Inc;

InnovationName: Computer Science
InnovationDescription: is responsible for developing the animation for making GIFs and other groundbreaking video technology such as Joost, Brightcove, Shockwave, and Hulu; 2016 co-founded and took on the role of Chief Executive Officer of tEQuitable, a start-up that provides an independent and confidential platform to address issues of bias, harassment, and discrimination in the workplace; invented Shockwave, a multimedia platform that laid the foundation for the modern web while Director of Program Management at Macromedia; helped to improve HealthCare.gov, reducing the number of individual pages and overall application time; she led the team that built the College Scorecard, an online tool for comparing the cost and value of higher education institutions in the United States; co-founded Emotient, which uses artificial intelligence to analyze facial expressions; co-founded Techturized Inc., a company whose mission is developing tech solutions specifically geared toward women of color;

InnovationName: Expert on the anatomy of wood & trees
InnovationDescription: studied southern pine trees & turpentine production; successfully developed methods to increase the yield & prolong the life of working trees; developed a program of "More turpentine, less scar, better pine"; during WWII wrote FPL wartime publications on defects in wood used for trainer aircraft and gliders; 1935 edited the comprehensive Naval Stores Handbook (201-pages) and contributed chapters on wood structure, physiology, and foreign naval stores production; breeder of Basenji's

InnovationName: Patented 1st Cotton Swabs
InnovationDescription: Received 2 patents for cotton swabs & 1 for a washrag/soap holder
Invention: Swab; Combined wash rag & soap holder

InnovationName: Electrical & Computer Engineering
InnovationDescription: working to make reliable ultra-fast wireless connectivity a reality; her research will enable devices like next-generation cellphones & autonomous vehicles; co-director of Princeton NextG industry affiliates program; led the tam that team developed a system that captures ripeness information from inside fruit using wireless signals that penetrate fruit peels without physically touching or damaging the fruit, they named the system AgriTera; founder of the Wireless Distinguished Seminar Series at Princeton;
Invention: Link Packing in mmWave networks; Managing analog beams in mmWave networks; MU-MIMO in mmWave systems
CoInventor: Narayan Prasad; Mohammad Khojastepour; Sampath Rangarajan

InnovationName: Discovered a black hole in the galactic center of the Milky Way
InnovationDescription: was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for the discovery of a black hole in the Milky Ways' galactic center; created the UCLA Galactic Center Group to coordinate research and technical developments; January 2020, her team reported the discovery of a new class of bizarre objects — objects that look like gas and behave like stars — at the center of our galaxy, not far from the supermassive black hole; helped pioneer a powerful technology called adaptive optics, which corrects the distorting effects of the Earth’s atmosphere in real time and opened the center of our galaxy as a laboratory for exploring black holes and their fundamental role in the evolution of the universe; published “You Can Be a Woman Astronomer” in 1995; took the first clear photo of the Milky Way; co-authored the book “The Galactic Center: A Window to the Nuclear Environment of Disk Galaxies;” developed a technique known as speckle imaging, which combines many short exposures from a telescope into a single, crisper image;

InnovationName: Inventor of The Gibbon Double Girder Lap-Joint Track
InnovationDescription: revolutionized the way train tracks were constructed with her invention, The Gibbon Double Girder Lap-Joint Track, constructed with just four main parts, greatly reduced the number of parts needed, helping to make construction more efficient;
Invention: Construction of side-bearing railway tracks; Construction of railway tracks; Compound rail for railway tracks

InnovationName: Mother of the Superfund
InnovationDescription: 1978 started the Love Canal Parents Movement; was a primary organizer of the Love Canal Homeowners Association who brought wide public attention to the environmental crisis in Love Canal; her actions resulted in the evacuation of 833 families; founded the non-profit Clearinghouse for Hazardous Waste in 1981 to help train and support local activists with their environmental work which was subsequently renamed the Center for Health, Environment, and Justice (CHEJ); has authored several books about the Love Canal story and the effects of toxic waste with the most quoted being "Love Canal. My story" written with Murray Levine and published in 1982 & 2 others-"Dying from Dioxin" (1995) & "Love Canal The Story Continues" (1998); her story was dramatized in the 1982 made-for-TV movie Lois Gibbs: the Love Canal Story, in which she was played by Marsha Mason*

InnovationName: Head of the Women's Centennial Exposition Committee
InnovationDescription: was the head of the Women's Centennial Exposition Committee; after being told there was no space in the main hall for a Women's Exhibition she & her committee took four months to raise more than $31,000 to erect the one-acre Woman’s Pavilion, the first at any world’s fair; her autobiography is titled "A Book of Remembrance"; 1893 as head of the Colonial Dames of Pennsylvania tried to get the city of Philadelphia to call June 14 Flag Day & it was officially enacted as Flag Day in 1937 with President Truman making it a National holiday in 1949*1883 with 27 other women formed The Associate Committee of Women of the Pennsylvania Museum and School of Industrial Art (1961 updated its name to The Women’s Committee of the Philadelphia Museum of Art);

InnovationName: Patented the 1st progressive lens
InnovationDescription: filed the patent for the first progressive lens (patent granted 1923); her work with Edgar Tillyer at the American Optical Company (now part of Carl Zeiss Vision) improved the optics of eyeglasses, cameras, telescopes, and military optical instruments; worked as a geometric optician with Tillyer for nearly 10 years, doing the mathematical work to develop the Tillyer corrected curve lens but didn't receive credit for her work; developed a breakthrough camera lens; 1946 she published a paper on "Practical Methods of Computing Finite Throw Schmidt Systems;" did considerable mathematical research on the theory of iseikonic systems especially focused on investigating the theory of variable magnification systems without change in focal power and applied this theory to variable size lenses;
Invention: Wide aperture lens system having means for reducing spherical aberrations; Size testing system; Opthalmic lens; Optical system for measuring changes in magnification; Lens testing instrument; Lens seating device; Lens; Lens-grinding machine; Wide aperture objective; Image projection optical system; Measuring device
CoInventor: Louis L. Gagnon; Edgar D. Tillyer; John K. Davis

InnovationName: Co-founder of the Providence Players
InnovationDescription: 1915 with her husband George Cram Cook, she founded the Provincetown Players, the first modern American theatre company; discovered playwright Eugene O'Neill; wrote numerous short stories (over 50 were published), nine novels, fifteen plays, and a biography; 1921 she completed "Inheritors" it follows three generations of a pioneer family and is often considered America's first modern historical drama; also in 1921 finished The Verge, one of the earliest American works of expressionist art; age 20 wrote ‘Society,’ a weekly that sarcastically criticized the upper-class

InnovationName: 2006 - Harnessing biological motors to engineer systems for nanoscale transport and assembly.
InnovationDescription: * Goel examines the physics of life and the way nanomotors read and write information into DNA * Development of novel conceptual frameworks and theoretical models to describe molecular nanomachines: the dynamics, energy transduction, and coupling to their environment * Experimentally probe the single molecule dynamics of molecular machines that read/write DNA * Demonstrate precision control of nanomotors that read/write DNA * Develop nanoscale techniques to precision control nanomachines and harness them for nanomanufacturing.
Invention: Single-molecule platform for drug discovery:  methods & apparatuses for drug discovery, including discovery of anticancer & antiviral agents; Systems & methods for mobile device analysis of nucleic acids & proteins; Nano biofuel production processes: using nanotechnology to enhance production for biofuels; Nano-PCR:  methods & devices for nucleic acid amplification & detection; Nanobiofuel production using nanoscale control methods & materials; Single-molecule platform for drug discovery:  methods for drug discovery, including discovery of anticancer & antiviral agents

InnovationName: Co-founder of the National Historical Publishing Company
InnovationDescription: co-founder of the National Historical Publishing Company, which is known for publishing historical maps; 1876 wrote "Minnesota, Its Geography, History, and Resources" & the text was considered groundbreaking for combining history, resources, and geography, an idea later used by other textbook publishers in the United States; before her marriage she was creator of historical wall maps that included historical events of countries; with husband Henry Slade Goff wrote "Goff's Historical Map of the Spanish-American War in the West Indies, 1898;" her collaboration with her husband produced over 100 historical maps, charts, and books, which included the historical atlas called "The United States and Her Neighbors" and the "Goff's Historical Map of the Philippine Islands;"her maps & annotations documented the world during her lifetime

InnovationName: Co-inventor of Smalltalk-80
InnovationDescription: was one of the co-developers of the programming language Smalltalk-80, which is a computer software that simplifies the programming language, and has been an influence on other programming languages such as Python, C, and Java; developed many concepts related to object-oriented programming; with Alan Kay was involved in the development of design templates, forerunners of the design patterns later used in software design; 1976 with Kay wrote the influential article "Personal Dynamic Media", which predicted a world in which ordinary individuals would use notebook computers to exchange, modify, and redistribute personal media; 1988 left PARC to cofound ParcPlace Systems, a company that created development tools for Smalltalk-based applications; 1999 cofounded Neometron, Inc. an Internet support provider; she co-wrote the seminal book on Smalltalk-80 with David Robson, another on the programming tools and user interface concepts, and a third with Kenneth Rubin on how the new technology impacts professional approaches to software development project management; co-founded AgileMind, a provider of Internet and classroom-based support for K-12 teachers and students;

InnovationName: Curator of the Studio Museum in Harlem
InnovationDescription: one of the originators of the term post-blackness; organized numerous innovative exhibitions of art by African-Americans & mentored the careers of numerous African-American artists; spearheaded the construction of the first-ever purpose-built facility in the Studio Museum’s history; helped produce the revolutionary 1993 Biennial and curated the groundbreaking exhibit Black Male, which examined destructive and persistent stereotypes about African-American masculinity;

InnovationName: Founder of the Christian Science Movement & Church
InnovationDescription: 1879 founded The Church of Christ, Scientist, the Mother Church of the Christian Science movement; founded The Christian Science Monitor in 1908, and three religious magazines: the Christian Science Sentinel, The Christian Science Journal, and The Herald of Christian Science; 1875 wrote "Science and Health with Key to the Scriptures;" authored "Manual of The Mother Church" and a collection of varied writings that were consolidated posthumously into a book called "Prose Works;" 1881 started the Massachusetts Metaphysical College with a charter from the state which allowed her to grant degrees; charged her students at the Massachusetts Metaphysical College $300 each for tuition-a very large sum for the time; founded The Christian Science Publishing Society in 1898, which became the publishing home for numerous publications launched by her and her followers; 1908, at the age of 87, she founded The Christian Science Monitor, a daily newspaper; founded the Christian Science Journal in 1883; 1898 founded the Christian Science Sentinel and the Herald of Christian Science; 1895 she published a church manual, establishing guidelines that are followed to this day;

InnovationName: Archaeology
InnovationDescription: most significant contributions to archaeology came from her skills as a strategist and analyst; the excavation of more than 280 graves near Halai allowed her to establish a clear chronology for the style of terracotta figures in the area; her brief excavation in Colophon revealed some of the earliest known Greek houses, a drainage system of terracotta pipes below the ancient streets, and a tomb with pottery of a late-Minoan design; her Tarsus excavation uncovered a miniature crystal statue of a fine and unusual Hittite design, as well as bilingual treaties and seals that demonstrated the history of the city’s rulers and written language; 1936 first woman to be appointed to the Institute for Advanced Study as a professor;

InnovationName: Inventor of the Crayon Holder
InnovationDescription: 1999 at age 11 invented the Crayon Holder to enable children to continue drawing with broken or stubs of crayons; with father, Norman Goldstein, founded By Kids For Kids Co (BKFK) which is dedicated to making the invention & commercialization process easy & accessible to all kids;
Invention: Device for holding a writing instrument; Device for holding writing instruments

InnovationName: Founder of Leanna's Inc
InnovationDescription: at age 9 founded Leanna's Hair a line of oils, conditioners, and hairdressing based on her Haitian great-grandmother's all natural recipe for hair products; 2013 at age 17 started a charitable organization called the Leanna Archer Education Foundation, which provides poverty-stricken children in Haiti with food and education that now provides services to 200 Haitian children; founder & CEO of Leanna's Inc at age 16

InnovationName: Invented magnetic wallpaper
InnovationDescription: age 14 invented magnetic locker wallpaper so she could decorate her school locker & not have to scrape things off at the end of the year

InnovationName: Mother of the Sitcom
InnovationDescription: one of the first women to create, write, produce, and star in a long-running hit when she premiered her radio serial comedy-drama The Rise of the Goldbergs (1929); the name of the show was later changed to The Goldbergs; published a best-selling memoir, Molly and Me, in 1961; "The Goldbergs" was one of the first programs to eschew sound "effects" in favor of the real thing, like running water and frying bacon; wrote The Molly Goldberg Cookbook (1955); is considered by some to be the Mother of the Sitcom;

InnovationName: Inventor of the Hot Seat & EasyFlo
InnovationDescription: at age 14 as a science fair project invented the Hot Seat a small pad with a sensor can be placed by parents under an infant’s booster or car seat & if the parent walks 20 feet away an alarm goes off to alert that there is an unattended child left in the vehicle; founder and CEO of the company Assila (her name spelled backwards); 2019 she announced a new invention, a baby bottle that stores water and dried formula separately, for mixing when needed (EasyFlo); 2019 CEO & founder of EasyFlo;
Invention: Vicinity monitor detector-based occupant detection & notification system

InnovationName: Invented a satchel made of recycled denim
InnovationDescription: invented & patented (none found) a hip satchel made out of old jeans

InnovationName: Wrote the manual for ENIAC
InnovationDescription: wrote the detailed Operators Manual for the ENIAC around 1945; was an instrumental player in converting the ENIAC from a computer that needed to be reprogrammed each time it was used to one that was able to perform a set of fifty stored instructions;

InnovationName: Computer Science
InnovationDescription: main achievement was the Blum-Goldwasser & Goldwasser-Micali cryptosystems; 2016 co-founder and chief scientist of Duality Technologies; research areas include computational complexity theory, cryptography and computational number theory; co-inventor of probabilistic encryption, which set up and achieved the gold standard for security for data encryption; co-inventor of zero-knowledge proofs, which probabilistically and interactively demonstrate the validity of an assertion without conveying any additional knowledge, and are a key tool in the design of cryptographic protocols; her work in number theory includes the invention with Joe Kilian of primality proving using elliptic curves; is a lead on Project CETI, an interdisciplinary initiative for translating the communication of sperm whales; inventor of several revolutionary cryptographic technologies including probabilistic encryption, multi-party secure protocols, and pseudo-random function;

InnovationName: Military Explosives
InnovationDescription: led the team that created the BLU-118/B, a laser-guided bomb designed to travel deep into confined spaces (AKA the Bunker Buster Bomb)( BLU stands for Bomb Live Unit); responsible for the creation of an American thermobaric weapon by leading a team of 100 scientists who developed & created 11 bombs within 67 days after 9/11;

InnovationName: Invented test for invasive amebiasis
InnovationDescription: patented processes to diagnose invasive amebiasis, a parasitic disease that kills over 100,000 people each year
Invention: Reportedly holds 2 patents in Mexico & 2 in the US but none were located

InnovationName: Co-inventor of Long-Cycle-Life Nickel-Hydrogen batteries
InnovationDescription: 1998, led the team that created the nickel-hydrogen batteries ( Long Cycle-Life Nickel-Hydrogen batteries) crucial for powering the International Space Station’s life support systems and scientific experiments; is an inventor of a patent directed at separator technology for alkaline batteries; work focused on energy storage technologies for improving space exploration; 2013 owner & founder of GS Matrix Consulting LLC
Invention: Alkaline battery containing a separator of a cross-linked copolymer of vinyl alcohol & unsaturated carboxylic acid
CoInventor: Li-Chen Hsu; Warren H. Philipp; Dean W. Sheibley

InnovationName: Discovered/named over 200 varieties of algae
InnovationDescription: discovered over 200 different algae species; compiled a book on marine algae of the Monterey peninsula, which later was expanded to include all of the California coast; authored eight books and over 150 publications; 1976 wrote "Marine Algae of California" the definitive study on Pacific Coast seaweed; established the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa's underground major of Ethnobotany;

InnovationName: Pioneer in Mossbauer spectroscopy
InnovationDescription: pioneered an experimental technique called Mössbauer spectroscopy, which uses gamma rays to figure out the molecular structure of complicated compounds containing metal ions; contributed to the understanding of catalysts such as ruthenium which activate or speed up chemical reactions; worked on processes of solvent extraction of metal complexes and described the chemical and physical properties of chemical species in an organic solvent; was able to explain why solutions of radioactive iodine were unstable, and determine the concentration at which species would be at equilibrium values, by applying the Nernst equation effect; did work in materials science on the physical and biological investigations of marine antifouling coatings, used to remove barnacles from ships; work included supervising a complete revision of the IUPAC nomenclature of inorganic chemistry or "Red Book;" was the founding Chairman of ASTRA, the Alliance for Science & Technology Research in America, beginning in 2000; authored more than 100 research papers in solvent separations and characterization of metallic species, solid-state chemistry and electron exchange, and testing methods for tin antifouling coatings; was the first to observe Mössbauer effects in ruthenium and its various oxidation states, contributing to the understanding of this important catalyst by deriving detailed chemical and structural information;
Invention: Cellulose acetate bound photosensitizer for producing singlet oxygen; Polysiloxane bound photosensitizer for producing singlet oxygen; Titanate bound photosensitizer for producing singlet oxygen
CoInventor: Stephen F. Yates; Inara M. Brubaker; Romulus Gaita

InnovationName: Social Activist
InnovationDescription: improved schools and libraries, started a juvenile court system, promoted education and rights for women, and challenged the racism of the Old South by pushing for social change; 1905 co-founded the Southern Association for College Women (later become the Arkansas Association for University Women a division of the American Association of University Women) which provided a forum for college educated women to discuss issues that were important to them; was an advocate of hiring professional school administrators and formed the first school improvement association in Arkansas; led efforts to provide transportation for rural students; 1911 was appointed by the local Women's Christian Temperance Union to investigate juvenile courts that had been established by legislation the group had championed; 1958 with Vivion Brewer and Velma Powell, founded the Women's Emergency Committee to Open Our Schools; formed the first School Improvement Association in Arkansas, forerunner of the Parent Teacher Association; organized the first juvenile court in Arkansas in 1910; chaired the Pulaski County Juvenile Court board for about twenty years; helped start the Girls Industrial School near Alexander (Pulaski and Saline Counties) for girls detained by the court, as well as a temporary home for young people who had no adult supervision; was instrumental in starting the Pulaski County Tuberculosis Association and the Community Chest, the forerunner of the United Way; worked to make Little Rock's auditorium accessible to older people and the handicapped;

InnovationName: Primatology
InnovationDescription: world's foremost expert on chimpanzees; discovered chimps make & use tools; 1960 discovered chimps are omnivorous; did chimp mother-infant study; discovered animals display complex social behavior such as altruism, affection & ritualized behavior; founder of the Jane Goodall Institute in California (1977) and the Roots & Shoots (1991) its youth program; discovered that chimpanzees will systematically hunt and eat smaller primates such as colobus monkeys; 1992 founded the Tchimpounga Chimpanzee Rehabilitation Centre in the Republic of Congo to care for chimpanzees orphaned due to bush-meat trade; 1994 founded the Lake Tanganyika Catchment Reforestation and Education (TACARE or "Take Care") pilot project to protect chimpanzees' habitat from deforestation by reforesting hills around Gombe while simultaneously educating neighboring communities on sustainability and agriculture training; TACARE project also supports young girls by offering them access to reproductive health education and through scholarships to finance their college tuition; in the mid-1990s, the Jane Goodall Institute's Center for Primate Studies was created at the University of Minnesota to house and organize the data she had collected over the years-in 2011 plans were made to transfer the data to Duke University; 2018 and 2020 she partnered with friend and CEO Michael Cammarata on two natural product lines from Schmidt's Naturals and Neptune Wellness Solutions with five percent of every sale benefited the Jane Goodall Institute; collaborated with NASA to use satellite imagery from the Landsat series to remedy the effects of deforestation on chimpanzees and local communities in Western Africa by offering the villagers information on how to reduce activity and preserve their environment; with Professor Mark Bekoff, founded the organization Ethologists for the Ethical Treatment of Animals in 2000; noted that chimpanzees throw stones as weapons, use touch and embraces to comfort one another and develop long-term familial bonds; observed that chimpanzees have a primitive "language" system containing more than 20 individual sounds; is also an accomplished photographer, and has published several books of her photographs;

InnovationName: Inventor of SkoBots
InnovationDescription: founded the STEAM Connection in 2019 when she was just eighteen; creates equitable and innovative learning solutions for Indigenous youths with robots that she designs, manufactures, and gives away for free; her flagship invention is Every Kid Gets a Robot (EKGAR), an innovative educational robotics kit that costs less than $20 dollars to make and is sent to youth for free, increasing their technical competency and understanding with a culturally competent curriculum; her invention the SkoBot is a personalized, wearable, and interactive Indigenous language revitalization robot that senses motion and speaks; in partnership with her friend Kevin Villanueva, an augmented reality designer with Chicano and youth-led group Lucid Skies LLC, she developed a virtual version of the SkoBot in the form of an Instagram filter that people can interact with on their phones; started a volunteer elementary school STEAM program called Benzene Buddies; summer of 2020 with Dr. Joshuaa Allison-Burbank created the fundraiser Books for Diné Bikéyah to bring Diné books to Diné youth living in Navajo Nation during the pandemic; has written & illustrated a series of five children's books to increase diverse STEM representation for young children that is distributed for free by The STEAM Connection; 2020 invented Twenty an affordable, simple, and creative open-source robotics kit that was created to increase students technical learning at home; started a weekly newsletter and wrote at-home coding lesson plans for parents to allow them to be a part of the learning process;

InnovationName: Founder of Girl Scouts of America
InnovationDescription: inspired by Robert Baden-Powell in 1912 established the first Girl Guide troop in the country in Savannah, Georgia & it became Girl Scouts of America in 1915; 1912 released the first American Girl Guides manual, entitled How Girls Can Help Their Country, a slightly amended version of Agnes Baden-Powell's book; 1913 set up the Girl Scouts national headquarters in Washington, D.C.; designed and patented the trefoil badge; formed the Honorary Committee of Girl Scouts and elected her family and friends to the committee; worked on and appeared in The Golden Eaglet, the first Girl Scout movie; after the 1922 convention she began planning Cloudlands, a camping facility in Cloudland, Georgia, designed to train leaders and girls together & it was later renamed Camp Juliette Low;
Invention: Liquid container for use with garbage cans or the like; Trefoil Girl Scout Badge; disposable drinking cup

InnovationName: Named the Hula Hoop & introduced it to the US
InnovationDescription: named the Hula hoop & introduced it to Wham-O & the US

InnovationName: Publishing
InnovationDescription: first woman elected to the board of the Associated Press; 1972 became the first female CEO of a Fortune 500 company, the Washington Post; held the title of publisher from 1969 to 1979, and that of chairwoman of the board from 1973 to 1991; supported reporters Bob Woodward and Carl Bernstein when they brought the Watergate story to the Post; was publisher when the Post defied the United States government to publish the classified Pentagon Papers; emphasizing freedom of the press, she strengthened the role of newspapers in exposing government actions;

InnovationName: Advertising
InnovationDescription: was "Aunt Jemima"; was one of the founding members of Olivet Baptist Church, the oldest active Black Baptist church in Chicago, was a minister and a philanthropist;

InnovationName: Native American Beadworker
InnovationDescription: is widely known for her fully beaded tennis shoes, which feature pictorial elements on solid, lane-stitched backgrounds; is a regular contributing writer to First American Art Magazine; was a co-curator of Hearts of Our People, a groundbreaking national traveling exhibition of Native American women’s art that opened in 2019; uses her beadwork to tell stories;

InnovationName: Inventor of Wristies
InnovationDescription: at age 10, inventor or Wristies, protective winter gear that are designed to be worn under your coat and gloves that block the snow, wind, and cold from entering any unprotected gaps, & founder of the company to market them (Wristies, Inc); 2001 made the US Rock Climbing Team and went to the World Cup in Imst, Austria; 2013 founded Millyardage LLC to sell USA made Polartec fabrics by the yard, uses the same fabric to make her Wristies;
Invention: Article of thermal clothing for covering the underlying area at the gap between a coat sleeve & a glove

InnovationName: Inventor/Game for Women
InnovationDescription: invented game, "Boys Scoot Over.  Girls Advance to the Top," "Tooth-Fairy Light" (a blinking light for children) & "SHHHH Machine" (a mechanism that uses a decibel meter to indicate when a classroom, for example, is getting too noisy);

InnovationName: Co-founder of Computer-Supported Cooperative Work
InnovationDescription: co-founder of the field of Computer-Supported Cooperative Work (CSCW) with Paul Cashman it is the science of interaction between people and their machines; 1988 edited "Computer-Supported Cooperative Work, A Book of Readings," the first book in the field; ran a team in the MIT Laboratory for Computer Science that developed systems to allow co-authoring and shared and real-time collaboration; she and her team produced Version Manager for the hugely successful 1-2-3 spreadsheet program; played a key role in the strategy for Domino, a Lotus web-based business collaboration suite that included enterprise-grade email, workflow and security features; her evangelism of synchronous communications, or chat, led to Sametime, Lotus’s real-time communications platform and the first channel for delivering Lotus Notes mail on the PalmPilot; 2007 her team, in partnership with IBM’s Visual Communications Lab, delivered Many Eyes, a service that connected groups to data graphics to help them collectively analyze information; her innovations include Reinvent Email, business activities, and social bookmarking;
Invention: Spreadsheet program which implements alternative range references`

InnovationName: Co-inventor of Roomba

InnovationName: Expert on Lead Poisoning
InnovationDescription: expert in occupational health & industrial toxicity; identified over 70 industrial processes in which workers were exposed to lead poisoning; wrote Industrial Poisons in the US.; 1910 Illinois governor Charles S. Deneen appointed her as a medical investigator to the newly formed Illinois Commission on Occupational Diseases; authored the "Illinois Survey," the commission's report that documented its findings of industrial processes that exposed workers to lead poisoning and other illnesses; uncovered occupations, such as polishing cut glass and wrapping cigars in "tinfoil," that exhibited increased exposure to lead poisoning, contrary to the public's beliefs; her best-known research included her studies on carbon monoxide poisoning among American steelworkers, mercury poisoning of hatters, and a debilitating hand condition developed by workers using jackhammers; 1934 published "Industrial Toxicology;" 1924 to 1930, she served as the only woman member of the League of Nations Health Committee; after retiring from Harvard in 1935 she became a medical consultant to the U.S. Division of Labor Standards; published her autobiography, Exploring the Dangerous Trades, in 1943; studied the poisonous effects of aniline dyes, carbon monoxide, mercury, tetraethyl lead, radium (in wristwatch dials among other uses), benzene, the chemicals in storage batteries, and carbon disulfide and hydrogen sulfide gases created in the manufacture of viscose rayon; founded the Alice Hamilton Club for teenage girls and a hygiene and nursing program as well as a well-baby clinic at Hull House; published 15 federal government reports, 17 books and pamphlets, and 165 articles;
